questions.title: Which television series will win Outstanding Comedy Series at the 2026 Primetime Emmy Awards?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The Television Academy's official winner announcement for Outstanding Comedy Series at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards in 2026. Resolution : Resolve when the winner in this category is formally announced. Accepted Answer Format : The title of the winning television series.
questions.current_reasoning: With 2025 champion The Studio ineligible this cycle, HBO Max's Hacks—airing its acclaimed fifth and final season—is the consensus frontrunner for Outstanding Comedy Series: it led early May trading odds at 59%, took #1 on Gold Derby on June 11 (97.7% nomination odds), and is Variety's predicted winner. Apple TV's Shrinking (Season 3) is the clearest runner-up with strong voter affection and campaign backing, followed by HBO's final-season revival The Comeback and star-studded Apple TV freshman Margo's Got Money Troubles (both ~13-14% in May markets), while Abbott Elementary remains a perennial top nominee with modest win equity.

questions.current_reasoning: With 2025 winner Britt Lower ineligible, Rhea Seehorn (Pluribus) is the unanimous #1 frontrunner (100% Gold Derby expert nomination odds as of June 23 and Variety's June 4 predicted winner), backed by an overwhelming 'overdue' narrative after Better Call Saul's 0-for-53 Emmy run and a rave-reviewed solo showcase. Keri Russell (The Diplomat, 6 previous nominations and 0 wins) is the clear #2 contender with strong overdue appeal, while Emmy legend Kathy Bates (Matlock) carries deep Television Academy goodwill. Two-time winner Zendaya (Euphoria) retains upset potential for her final season, though minimal campaigning and divisive Season 3 backlash weaken her three-peat odds, and Carrie Coon (The Gilded Age) rounds out the top five ahead of Gotham winner Chase Infiniti.

questions.title: Who will win Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate?
questions.background: Michigan will elect a U.S. senator in November 2026. The Democratic primary will determine the party’s nominee for that election.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Results from Michigan election authorities or unambiguous reporting by major news organizations identifying the winner of Michigan’s 2026 Democratic primary for U.S. Senate. Resolution Date : Resolve when the winner of the primary, scheduled for August 4, 2026, is publicly established. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate’s name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major race-reshaping update on 2026-07-05: State Sen. Mallory McMorrow suspended her Michigan U.S. Senate campaign without endorsing either rival, turning the Aug. 4 Democratic primary into a head-to-head race between Abdul El-Sayed and Rep. Haley Stevens (removing McMorrow's prior 0.14). Two major late-June polls published since our June 24 forecast showed El-Sayed pulling solidly ahead while McMorrow faded into single digits: Mitchell Research (mid-June) had El-Sayed 42%, Stevens 33%, McMorrow 6% (+9), and Quantus Insights (June 29-30, published July 2) had El-Sayed 41%, Stevens 36%, McMorrow 8% (+5). El-Sayed also landed Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's endorsement on July 2 (her first in a contested 2026 Senate primary) alongside Bernie Sanders and UAW grassroots labor backing, amid recent progressive primary wins in NY and CO. While McMorrow's exit stops the Oakland County suburban split and her remaining 6-8% voters likely lean modestly toward Stevens (~60/40, offset by Warren/Murphy/anti-Schumer voters going to El-Sayed), El-Sayed still projects ~3-5 points ahead head-to-head. Discounting slightly for Stevens's ~$8M+ AIPAC/establishment super PAC paid-media blitz, older/Black high-propensity primary turnout edge, and 30 days remaining (including the WOOD TV8 debate), we shift El-Sayed to 0.56 (+0.14) and hold Stevens at 0.43 (leaving 0.01 residual tail).

local_articles.title: Democrats Haley Stevens and Abdul El-Sayed face off in primary debate for Michigan Senate
local_articles.snippet: Michigan's remaining Democratic Senate candidates — Rep. Haley Stevens and former Michigan health official Abdul El-Sayed — are set to go head to head in a televised debate Tuesday, two days after state Sen. Mallory McMorrow suspended her campaign. Bernie Sanders of Vermont and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez of New York. The primary between Stevens and El-Sayed is Aug. 4, with the winner advancing to compete against former GOP Rep. local_articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed, Haley Stevens to meet in Democratic U.S. Senate debate
local_articles.snippet: Within days of state Sen. Mallory McMorrow announcing she was suspending her campaign for Michigan's open U.S. Senate race, Abdul El-Sayed and Michigan U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens will square off in a televised debate. The debate featuring the two remaining Democratic candidates for Michigan's closely watched Senate race is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET Tuesday. The debate pits El-Sayed, the former director of the Wayne County Department of Health, Human and Veterans Services and a 2018 Democratic gubernatorial primary candidate, against Stevens, a four-term member of the U.S. House representing the state's 11th District. El-Sayed and Stevens will square off in the Aug. 4 primary for the Democratic nomination. Former Rep. Mike Rogers is the sole Republican listed on the GOP primary ballot. questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: July 4-5 reporting (Al Jazeera, Straits Times/Bloomberg, Khaleej Times) from the World Peace Forum in Beijing meaningfully strengthens Oman's lead as Iran's most likely bilateral partner on Strait of Hormuz clearance/management. Speaking July 4—five days after Oman's Sultan Haitham met Macron in Paris—Iranian Ambassador to China Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli explicitly reaffirmed that Iran is working in 'collaboration and cooperation' with Oman on 'new arrangements' for 'guaranteeing the security of passage' through the strait, and Al Jazeera confirmed Iran and Oman have established a formal joint committee to manage the waterway (even as at least eight ships turned back along the Omani coast July 3-4). This resolves our July 1 concern that Tehran's anti-France demining rebuke (reiterated July 1 by Africanews) had sidelined Oman. Conversely, Bloomberg noted that China—though promised 'special considerations' on future transit fees—has kept to the sidelines of the conflict, merely calling July 3 for unhindered shipping and relying diplomatically on Pakistan. We raise Oman (0.26 -> 0.32) while trimming China (0.25 -> 0.23), Pakistan (0.18 -> 0.17), and Russia (0.14 -> 0.12), keeping Japan at 0.03 (sum 0.87, leaving 13% tail for Qatar, India, Turkey, UAE, etc.).

questions.title: Which company will be the world's most valuable publicly traded company by market capitalization on July 17, 2026?
questions.background: Market capitalization is the total market value of a company's outstanding shares.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the company identified as the world's most valuable by market capitalization in Al Jazeera's contemporaneous reporting on July 17, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-07-17 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the company's commonly used name.
questions.current_reasoning: CompaniesMarketCap data reported June 24 placed Nvidia at $4.845T ahead of Apple ($4.322T), Alphabet ($4.223T), Microsoft ($2.812T), and SpaceX ($2.254T). On June 25, Apple shares tumbled 5.0%-5.6% (to ~$4.08T-$4.10T) after shocking global 20%-42% MacBook/iPad price hikes driven by AI memory chip shortages, while Nvidia fell >2% (to ~$4.73T, amid tech rotation and OpenAI's custom 'Jalapeno' inference chip unveiled with Broadcom) and Alphabet fell ~1% (to ~$4.18T). With only 15 US trading days remaining until July 17 (before Big Tech Q2 earnings), Nvidia holds a ~13.2% lead over #2 Alphabet and a widened ~15.6% lead over #3 Apple; correlated lognormal/t-tail modeling plus idiosyncratic AI sentiment risk puts Nvidia at 84%, Alphabet at 11%, Apple down to 4%, and Microsoft/SpaceX at 0.5% each.

local_articles.title: Samsung tops Nvidia with record Q2 operating profit
local_articles.snippet: Samsung Electronics appears to have overtaken Nvidia to post the world’s largest quarterly operating profit among major tech companies, reporting a record 89.4 trillion won ($58.6 billion) for the second quarter on booming demand for AI memory chips. Samsung said Tuesday its preliminary operating profit for the April-June period surged 1,810.3 percent from a year earlier. Revenue jumped 129.3 percent on-year to an all-time high of 171 trillion won. The operating profit also beat the market consensus of 84.16 trillion won compiled by Yonhap Infomax by 6.2 percent. The latest figure marks a 56 percent jump from Samsung’s previous record of 57.2 trillion won set in the first quarter, when it became the first Korean company to top 50 trillion won in quarterly operating profit.
